theme-park game sourced

Theme Park

A theme park management game in which the player builds rides and shops, tunes prices and recipes for individually simulated visitors, and sells parks to expand worldwide.

1994Bullfrog ProductionsManagement / tycooncluster c0114 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

place rides, shops, and paths -> visitors arrive by bus and choose attractions -> tune prices and shop ingredients -> fund research and hire staff -> yearly judging against rivals -> sell the park and buy a plot abroad

design notes

Theme Park gives every visitor its own record (about 200 bytes each) and lets the player change the product as well as its price: ingredient settings such as sugar in ice cream trade cost against whether customers return. The full-simulation level adds wage and supply negotiations, where failure means staff strikes or lost shipments, plus research funding and shares; the sandbox level removes them, so one engine serves three depths. Unhappy visitors attract thugs, which ties satisfaction to crime. Negotiation has no mechanic in the taxonomy (proposed as negotiation).

uses

Crowd preferences

Each visitor is an individual with its own personality and arrives and leaves by bus; unhappy crowds draw thugs who vandalize and attack entertainers.

core
uses

Customer value choice

Entry, ride, and shop prices plus ingredient levels such as sugar in ice cream decide what visitors buy and whether they come back.

core
uses

Building placement

Over thirty attractions, shops, toilets, and scenery are placed on a plot, with coasters needing laid-out track.

core
uses

Staff hiring and rosters

Entertainers, security guards, mechanics, and handymen are hired and their wages negotiated; understaffing brings litter, breakdowns, and crime.

core
uses

Wear and breakdown

Rides wear down and explode if mechanics do not maintain them; research can make rides more durable.

core
uses

Crime and policing

Thugs appear when visitors are unhappy; security guards counter them.

On the full-simulation level, staff wage talks and supply negotiations are haggles; failed wage talks end in strikes and failed supply talks in lost shipments.
